name: Procyanidin oral (melasma)
lead: Oral procyanidin combined with vitamins A, C and E is an antioxidant supplement regimen tested for melasma, a condition of brown or gray-brown facial patches. People interested in it want a pill that evens out facial pigmentation from the inside, as a complement to sunscreen and topical lighteners, for a clearer and more uniform complexion.

The main published study is an 8-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial by Handog and colleagues in Manila, published in 2009 in the International Journal of Dermatology. It enrolled 60 women with bilateral epidermal melasma (Fitzpatrick skin types III to V), and 56 finished.[2] Instrument readings showed reduced pigmentation in both cheek regions and MASI scores improved, and the regimen was described as safe and well tolerated with minimal adverse events.[2] Wikipedia lists it among oral options for melasma.[1]

Dermatology reviews describe melasma as a chronic, recurrence-prone condition where no single treatment is universally effective and combinations often perform best.[3] The oral procyanidin regimen has no independent replication located here.

paras: Oral agents for melasma named by Wikipedia include tranexamic acid, procyanidin with vitamins A, C and E, and, from a systematic review, Polypodium leucotomos extract, beta-carotenoids and melatonin, which the review found effective with few and mild adverse events [1]. Standard care generally centers on topicals, sun avoidance and broad-spectrum sunscreen [1].

Standard care for melasma generally centers on topicals, sun avoidance and broad-spectrum sunscreen.[1] Looksmax.org threads on skin lightening and melasma compile treatment lists drawn from review tables, with oral agents such as Polypodium leucotomos appearing among them.[4]

The Handog 2009 trial randomized 60 adult women with bilateral epidermal melasma to oral procyanidin with vitamins A, C and E or placebo, taken twice daily with meals for 8 weeks; 56 completed. Mexameter pigmentation readings fell significantly in the left and right malar regions, MASI scores improved in both, and treatment was safe and well tolerated with minimal adverse events.[2] Wikipedia summarizes it as showing significant improvement in the malar regions.[1]

A 2022 systematic review of melasma treatments reports that tranexamic acid and Polypodium leucotomos had promising results, that recurrence is high across treatments, and that combination therapy performed best.[3]

Procyanidins are polyphenols found in plants such as French maritime pine bark, and are described as having antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; the trial paper does not itself establish how the regimen reduces pigment.[2]

timeline.event: Handog and colleagues publish an 8-week placebo-controlled trial of oral procyanidin with vitamins A, C and E in Filipino women with melasma.[2]

lore.intro: Oral options for melasma and skin lightening are discussed on looksmax.org in lists compiled from review articles, mainly alongside topical agents.[4]

claims.claim: Oral antioxidants can help lighten melasma
claims.believers: Forum users compile oral and topical lightening options from review tables and choose by side-effect profile.[4]
claims.experts: One small placebo-controlled trial reported lower pigmentation readings on the cheeks with procyanidin plus vitamins A, C and E; no replication has been published to date in the sources reviewed.[2]

card.summary: An antioxidant pill combo with one small placebo-controlled melasma trial reported, and little else.
card.aka: procyanidin with vitamins A, C, E
card.note: Evidence rests on a single 56-person trial as summarized on Wikipedia.

quick.overview:
This is a supplement combining procyanidin, a plant polyphenol, with vitamins A, C and E, tested for melasma.

One 8-week placebo-controlled trial in 56 women reported improvement on the cheeks. No other studies were found.
quick.mechanism: The sources reviewed do not describe how it would act; antioxidant activity is the usual proposed basis for such combinations.
quick.risks: The trial summary describes the regimen as safe and well tolerated. Long-term safety data were not found.

chain: Oral antioxidant procyanidin with vitamins A, C, E
Reduced pigmentation readings on the cheeks in one trial
angle.text: People with melasma take oral antioxidants hoping to lighten cheek patches and even out skin tone. In the one published trial, pigmentation readings and MASI scores on the cheeks improved over eight weeks.
